Justice in the City

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate corruption in our justice system...

Summary:
In conjunction with the Hawks, we set a trap and for alleged corrupt court officials to try and make an existing criminal case disappear. The trap was successful and over the next few days 7 people were arrested ranging from a cleaner to a senior prosecutor at Randburg Court, as well as two policemen. We will interview the head of Randburg Court, the Gauteng Police Commissioner and the investigating officer. We will also have an interview with an anonymous person (our informer) telling us how many times he knows of where these people have been "fixing" court cases.

Extra Budget Items:
I would like to apply for an investigative rate, as this investigation took more than 20 shooting days to complete.

Locations:
Gauteng

Hidden Camera: Yes
Reason for hidden camera: To film first attempts to set up the trap. Also for use during the successful trap

Legal: Yes
Reason for legal: 7 people were arrested. They will have appeared for bail application before broadcast, but he case will only be heard after broadcast. I'd like to clarify issues around whose faces i'm allowed to show and who i need to block out.

Press Release:


Justice for Sale
Criminals who make case dockets disappear, quite literally get away with murder. All that’s needed is a corrupt police officer and a greedy court official to see a case permanently removed from the court roll and the threat of jail time nullified. Carte Blanche joins forces with the authorities as we investigate and follow through our leads to the arrest of several high-ranking court officials accused of making cases disappear for a fee.


Script:


Dockets: Justice for sale

Studio link


When criminals and corrupt members of the SAPS work together this threatens the essence of a democratic society. Dockets go missing, evidence disappears and scores of criminals end up back in business instead of behind bars. cases are thrown out of court because of botched investigations or other unnecessary factors So, we trust the courts – but hundreds of cases are thrown out of court due to botched investigations or other interference.
Link 1: Claire in court
It's not all that bad, because if cases are still being thrown out of court it proves that our justice system is still functioning and protecting us... unless you find corrupt court officials.
V/o:
We've been hearing stories for a while about corrupt officials at the Randburg Magistrates court, so in February we decided to set a trap. Without trying too hard we found a fixer, a person claiming that, for a few rands he could make your court case disappear. He made a few phone calls from our vehicle and ended up speaking to a woman called Caroline at the court.
Up sound Informant
FIXER: Caroline, I'm so broke now, and I want to make some money. I'm with another friend here, and he's got 2 cases there, one drug one and once drinking and driving one. So I said to him that I can make a plan. Hello?

CAROLINE: Did you speak to Neo?

FIXER: Neo's not answering.

CAROLINE: Okay let me just ask her to call you now.

FIXER: Who, Neo?

CAROLINE: Yes

FIXER: Okay

V/o
Ten minutes later his phone rang.
Up sound Informant
ELIZABETH: Caroline told me to call you back, regarding your matter.
FIXER: Who?
ELIZABETH: Drinking and driving. Caroline.
FIXER: Ja
ELIZABETH: She said she can help you.
FIXER: Who's speaking?
ELIZABETH: It's Elizabeth.
FIXER: Okay, so listen here. How much will you charge my friend?
ELIZABETH: She said it's going to be 3 each.
FIXER: R3000 for each. Is that the best price?
ELIZABETH: Yes
FIXER: Okay, but listen here I'm going to get everything. But listen here but this friend here, he is very paranoid and he doesn't want to go to jail and stuff like that. So what he's also asking me is, when he gives me the money and I hand over the money to you will he get the docket and stuff like that?
ELIZABETH: Yes, okay.
FIXER: Is that fine?
ELIZABETH: Ja.
V/o:
They decided to set up a meeting with Caroline in a parking lot opposite Cresta Mall in Johannesburg West to make the payment in exchange for documentation proving that she kept her side of the bargain
She arrived with and our fixer got into their car. When she said that she didn't bring the proof he only paid R1500, saying that his client would pay the other half when he received proof. She gave him R500 back as his fee for the deal.
Upsound in Vehicle
FIXER: If Neo calls me, for example, I just say...

CAROLINE: No don't tell them anything. Just keep it like that.
Link2: In parking lot
The problem is that now we're on the verge of breaking the law ourselves, because we're buying an existing docket from a corrupt official.
V/o:
So we decided to work with the Hawks. They assigned Detective Warrant officer Ben “Bliksem” Booyens to our case who in 2013 was awarded the top cop award by the Hawks Ben has been with the police for 36 years.

With legal permission to set the trap, we set up the second meeting. Caroline told the fixer to come to her office but once again did not have proof to give him. So, he refused to give her the balance.
V/o
He told me that this was typical of how they stretch the process out to extort more money. But said in the end Caroline would deliver.

And true enough; ahead of the next meeting she pushed the price up to R5000.
FIXER
Depending on what type of client I'm bringing, I mean, if they meet the client, they can see if it's a rich white person. I mean they're going to milk it, milk it till the end.

CLAIRE: They feel that those clients are more desperate and they've got the means to pay more money?

Yes, because they're scared to go to jail. For a fact I've done this before. I mean for stupid cases we've charged the people up to R30,000 for something I'd charge a black and coloured person R3000 for.
V/o
Last week we set up a third meeting, in the same parking lot as the first one. While waiting, we twice saw an unmarked police vehicle driving suspiciously slowly through the parking lot. Its just as well that Ben to use the JMPD crime prevention unit in stead of SAPS members to assist him
V/o
When Caroline arrived, the fixer got into her car with the cash. She was not happy that he only brought R3000.

UPSOUND VEHICLE
CAROLINE: To withdraw a case doesn't take 5 minutes. If somebody comes and you give that person money so they'll withdraw your case you don't see anything. That person is playing with you.
V/o
But she handed him a warrant and took his money. When the deal was done and she wanted to leave , she found herself blocked off by police cars.
UPSOUND arrest
You're under arrest...
V/o
Rachel works as a cleaner at the court, and she is allegedly an accomplice as she had the money on her. She was also with Caroline when the first payment was made. Ben first thought that she was Caroline.
UPSOUND CHECKING MONEY
BEN: You see? The same. That's number one. 3982, 3982. You see the money that he gave you, the money that I gave him for the entrapment.

RACHEL: I didn't know.

BEN: It's police money. No, I don't know you didn't know. Because if you did know you wouldn't be so stupid to take it. Hey, Mama?

BEN: So, you are actually selling this?

CAROLINE: No, Zakele asked me to give it to this guy.

BEN: Who's Zakele?

CAROLINE: The one that works as the head of the criminal
V/o
Caroline and Rachel, were taken to Fairland police station. Ben's wife, Christel, a police colonel, helped with the arrests and taking statements.
V/o
In her statement Caroline named two police officers and 3 other people from the court she said were involved.
Link at Linden police station
It turned into a late night, but early on thursday morning, Ben and the JMPD squad arrived here at Linden police station to arrest the two suspects that Caroline had identified.
V/o
One of them, it turned out, was on duty the previous evening and allegedly the cop who cased out the parking lot just before the deal went down. The second policeman later handed himself over at Fairland station.
V/o
Court arrests sequence
Ben and co then went to the court to make the other arrests. One of three colleagues that Caroline named was Zakele.
UPSOUND
BEN: Do you understand your rights?
ZAKELE: What have I done?

V/o
Second to be arrested was Elizabeth, the woman who arranged the price with the fixer.
Link at Randburg court, in front of Modorodondo office
This is the office of the suspected kingpin, a prosecutor, who while seeing other arrests being made, made a run for it.
V/o:
Friday morning at Fairland
Later this prosecutor, named Mxolisi, informed Ben through his lawyer that he would hand himself over at Fairland Police station before noon the next day, Friday.
V/o:
We waited for three hours, he didn't arrive. His lawyer sent a message saying he was very stressed out and suicidal, but would hand himself over on Sunday morning at ten
V/o:
Sunday sequence
At 11 o clock he arrived with his lawyer, very anxious.
UPSOUND
BEN: The way that you kept staying away, it's not in your favour. So I'm glad that you came today. You understand?
Link at Randburg court.
This is the type of story where you hope to fail in what you set out to prove. But now that the corruption has reached our courts, where does this leave us?
V/o
Pieter Erasmus is the senior prosecutor at Randburg court and he agrees that this is not an isolated incident.
Interview Pieter Erasmus
I think it would be naïve to say that the situation and the recent arrests that took place in Randburg is unique to Randburg. It is a problem that dockets sometimes go missing and obviously that delays the process of getting matters to finality in a proper way.

CLAIRE: Can a case be made to disappear completely?

PIETER: It can happen that a matter disappears in the sense of it goes back to the police station. If nobody else attends to it might go undetected.
V/o:
While this expose leaves great cause for concern, the seriousness with which both Ben and Pieter treated our information left us with some hope. For the Hawks it is a priority to root out corruption in government
Interview SAPS
I think from our side we're very disappointed, disappointed in the fact that you have members of the police that are involved in corrupt activities. So, when people are arrested for corruption, even if it is one person, it does make a huge dent on the name of the organisation.
Closing link at Johannesburg court
At this point all seven suspects have been granted bail and are presumed innocent until the court rules otherwise. Ben's investigation continues and we'll keep you posted.
Interview Fixer
Ja, at Randburg court there was 5 arrested but unfortunately they're short another 5.

CLAIRE: Another 5?

FIXER: Yes. At Randburg Court they're short another 5. That I know for a fact. But there are probably more. But I know for a fact that there's another 5 that are short.
